records.name: Audubon Mid-Atlantic
records.summary: The Mid-Atlantic office of the National Audubon Society. In Philadelphia it runs the Discovery Center at the Strawberry Mansion Reservoir and leads public bird walks and tours in city parks.
records.what_you_do: Join a public birding walk or tour in a Philadelphia park, or visit the Discovery Center for its programs, such as nature journaling, stargazing, and habitat enhancement days.

schedule.text: Public birding walks and tours in Philadelphia parks are posted on the events calendar, each with its own sign-up link. The Discovery Center keeps its own hours, which change with the seasons.

locations.label: Walks and tours in city parks, such as FDR Park, The Woodlands, and East Fairmount Park

first_step.how: Pick a walk on the Audubon events calendar and register through its sign-up link.
first_step.basis: Walks are open to the public with a published sign-up link. The page does not say whether beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Walks listed for Philadelphia have run from 8 to 10 am in city parks such as FDR Park and The Woodlands. The page does not give a price, a group size, or what to bring, so read the listing before you go.
first_visit_tips: Summer hours end on Oct 15. After that the Discovery Center opens Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 5 pm, and it is closed Mondays.
Call the Discovery Center at (610) 990-3431 with questions, since its page lists no email.
Parking and directions are on a separate Audubon page, which names no SEPTA stop.

records.notes: Binoculars claim from tier 1 removed: the Discovery Center's own page does not say it lends binoculars and lists no exhibits or trails, so those amenities appear only in other listings. The Discovery Center address and phone come from its own page. The Mid-Atlantic get-involved page lists no Philadelphia volunteer roles. The Audubon events page returned a 404, and the Mobilize page for the Discovery Center walk returned only its title, so walk details rest on the main Mid-Atlantic page. Admission, accessibility, parking and transit are not stated on any page read.

records.name: Aurora Classical
records.summary: Puts on classical concerts at low cost, and runs a Classical Open Mic Matinee where musicians can perform for an audience. It also runs a free grocery bag pop-up for neighbors.
records.what_you_do: Come to a concert, sign up to play at the open mic, or email the group to volunteer or ask for a grocery bag.

schedule.text: Concerts and the Classical Open Mic Matinee are listed by date on the home page, held at the Philadelphia Ethical Society and other venues. The free grocery bag pop-up runs on the second Monday of each month.

cost.text: Some concerts are pay what you wish. Prices for other events are not listed.

first_step.how: Come listen to the Classical Open Mic Matinee, or email admin@auroraclassical.org to ask about playing.
first_step.basis: Concerts and the open mic are public. The home page says performers may play any classical piece and listeners are welcome, but it does not say beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: At the Classical Open Mic Matinee, performers play any classical piece with a pianist provided, and people can also come just to listen. The page does not say how long a slot lasts or how to book one, so email the group first.
first_visit_tips: Check the home page for the date and venue before you go.
The open mic listed for Oct 17, 2026 is at the Philadelphia Ethical Society, 1906 Rittenhouse Square. Venues can change, so check the listing.
Email admin@auroraclassical.org with questions about playing or about the grocery bags.

records.notes: The group's upcoming-events page read back September 2025 listings, while the home page lists 2026 events, including the Oct 17, 2026 open mic and a 2026 Fringe event, so the record follows the home page. The mailing address (c/o CultureTrust, 1315 Walnut St., Suite 300, Philadelphia, PA 19107) is not a venue and is not in the record. No phone is published. The open mic sign-up method is not stated beyond email. Accessibility, parking and transit are not stated. The grocery pop-up has no specific dates on the home page.

records.name: AUTOMAT Collective
records.summary: An artist run gallery in the Crane Arts Building that shows invited exhibitions and hosts free zinemaking workshops and book launches.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery on a Saturday, RSVP for a free zinemaking workshop, or come to a second Thursday reception or a book launch.

schedule.text: Gallery open Saturdays noon to 5 pm or by appointment. Second Thursday receptions run 6 to 9 pm each month.

locations.label: Gallery in Crane Arts Building, Suite 105

cost.text: Zinemaking workshop is free; RSVP required

access.notes: The gallery is wheelchair accessible and offers free handicap parking. The group's about page says it can be reached by car, bike, and public transit.

first_step.how: Come to a Saturday gallery visit, or RSVP through the group's Eventbrite link for a free zinemaking workshop such as Print and Play.
first_step.basis: The gallery is open to the public on Saturdays with no sign-up. Workshops take an RSVP, but the page does not say beginners are welcome or who a workshop is for.
first_step.what_to_expect: The gallery is the first gallery past the main front doors on the first floor of the Crane Arts Building. Visits run Saturdays from noon to 5 pm, and the page does not say how long a visit takes or who staffs the space.
first_visit_tips: Come on a Saturday between noon and 5 pm, or email the gallery to set up another time.
The gallery has free handicap parking and can be reached by car, bike, or public transit.
Print and Play is held at Second State Press, not at the gallery. The page gives no address for that venue, so read the RSVP details.

records.notes: Zip changed from 19125 to 19122 because the group's exhibition page gives 19122 and its home page lists both. The Print and Play workshop is held at Second State Press, not the gallery, per the group's own pages. The Eventbrite RSVP page was not read (lead platform). Workshop materials, age limits and gallery admission are not stated. Second State Press has no URL on the pages read, so it is not added as a lead.

records.name: Awbury Arboretum Food Forest Work Days
records.summary: Volunteers who help look after the food forest at Awbury Arboretum in Germantown. Planting and orchard care work days are listed through the Philadelphia Orchard Project, and Awbury's volunteer office takes questions by email.
records.what_you_do: Help plant and care for trees and plants on a listed work day. Register on the Philadelphia Orchard Project events page for the date.

schedule.text: Work days are posted by date on the Philadelphia Orchard Project events page. Check there for the next one.

locations.label: Awbury office, The Francis Cope House (mailing address)

cost.text: No fee is listed for work days.

first_step.how: Register for an upcoming work day on the Philadelphia Orchard Project events page with the Register Now button, or email volunteer@awbury.org to ask about other ways to help.
first_step.basis: The Philadelphia Orchard Project listing says volunteers of all ages and skill levels are welcome at planting and orchard care events, and that registering gets you directions.
first_step.what_to_expect: A work day is a morning session, such as 9 am to noon, spent helping care for the food forest. The listing does not say what tools or clothing to bring, who leads the day, or whether children may come, so ask when you register.
first_visit_tips: Register first. RSVPing is how you get the detailed directions and updates.
The food forest is at 6336 Ardleigh St, a different address from the Awbury office on One Awbury Road.
One Awbury page shows a volunteer phone number that differs by one digit from the main number, so email volunteer@awbury.org first if you are unsure which to call.

records.notes: Phone: the group's contact page lists 215-849-2855 as its only number, so that is kept. The volunteer page, read twice, showed 215-843-2855 for volunteer questions; that differs by one digit and needs confirming by a call or email. The awbury.org/contact-us page returned a 404, so the contact page was read instead. The volunteer page describes no steps, forms, orientation or minimum age, and it does not describe the work day itself. Access and transit are not stated. The POP events page also lists a Horticulture Center food forest workday (Oct 14) and a Penn Park orchard workday (Oct 28); neither is an Awbury event, so neither is recorded. Schedule days and times reflect the Oct 14 listing only.

records.name: Azuka Theatre Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that stages productions and develops new plays with writers. Its New Play Development program offers readings, events, and a way to submit scripts.
records.what_you_do: See a production and pay what you decide afterward, come to a New Play event when one is listed, or send a script through the online New Play Development form. The site does not describe classes, usher volunteering, or open rehearsals, so ask the company.

schedule.text: The company runs a season of productions, each with its own dates on the calendar, and lists a 2026 to 2027 season. New Play events are readings and workshops, announced when they are scheduled.

locations.label: The Theaters at The Drake (Louis Bluver Theatre or Proscenium Theatre)

cost.text: Pay What You Decide: reserve a seat for free, see the show, then pay the amount you choose. Fixed-price tickets are also sold.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: the B Line subway to Walnut-Locust, about 2 blocks from the theaters, per the company's directions page. The L Line stops at 15th Street, and several bus routes stop nearby.

first_step.how: Reserve a Pay What You Decide seat online or by phone for the next production, then pay the amount you choose after the show.
first_step.basis: Anyone can reserve a flexible-price seat with an email confirmation, and the New Play program takes work from emerging Philadelphia writers. The page does not say how a first visit works.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shows are at The Theaters at The Drake on South Hicks Street. For Pay What You Decide, you reserve a seat in advance at no cost, check in at the box office under your name, and pay after the show by cash, check, card, or Venmo. Unclaimed seats are released 15 minutes before each performance, so arrive early.
first_visit_tips: Check the production page to see which theater door to use, since both theaters are on Hicks Street.
Reserve early, because unclaimed seats are released 15 minutes before the show.
Take the B Line to Walnut-Locust, about 2 blocks away, or check the directions page for bus and trolley stops.
Pay after the show using the envelope basket or the box office.

records.notes: The #CHARLOTTESVILLE production (Oct 14 to Nov 1) appears on the home page with no year beside its dates, so it is not in the record and was removed from schedule text. The 2026 to 2027 season heading is written with its year and is used. The New Play events page lists no events yet. The New Play submission form asks for an artistic statement, a play synopsis, and a ten-page dialogue sample. No fee, no submission window, and no file format are shown, and responses can take up to a year. Accessibility (step-free entry, ASL, captions, audio description) is not stated. The footer names four resident companies (Interact Theatre, Inis Nua Theatre, Simpatico Theatre, PlayPenn) with no links, so none is added as a lead.

records.name: Sankofa Community Farm at Bartram's Garden
records.summary: The farm at Bartram's Garden, a 50-acre public park in Southwest Philadelphia. Sankofa Community Farm grows food with an African Diaspora focus and invites volunteers to help with seasonal planting and outdoor work.
records.what_you_do: Work with farm staff on seasonal plantings and outdoor care such as weeding, cleaning, pruning, and light maintenance. No special skills are needed. Anyone under 18 may help alongside a parent or guardian.

schedule.text: Sankofa Community Farm volunteer days are on Saturday mornings, 9:30 am to noon, and are posted on the garden's calendar. The Welcome Center is open Thursday to Monday, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm, from April into early December.

cost.text: Admission is free and most programs are free. Some paid events are offered.

access.notes: A wheelchair is available at the Welcome Center. Lath House restrooms have accessible stalls but no automatic doors. The Bartram's Mile Trail is paved with some moderate inclines, and the Meadow has grass paths with steeper slopes. Some areas offer audio descriptions for visitors with limited vision.

first_step.how: Register for a Sankofa Community Farm volunteer day on the garden's event page, where you sign your own waiver. Welcome Volunteer applications are closed, so you can join the interest list instead.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says no special skills or past experience are needed, and it walks through how to register and sign the waiver.
first_step.what_to_expect: A volunteer day runs from 9:30 am to noon on a Saturday and meets at the farm at Bartram's Garden. The work is outdoors with farm staff, such as planting, harvesting, weeding, removing invasive plants, and helping the orchard, and no special skills are needed. The listing does not say what to bring or wear or whether tools are supplied, so check the event page before you go.
first_visit_tips: Register on the event page first and sign your own waiver, since each person registers separately.
Public restrooms are open daily, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm.
Parking is free in the loop from 54th Street, along 51st Street, and along 56th Street, but on-site spots are limited.

records.notes: Welcome Volunteer applications are closed, so that program is interest-list only. Its requirements, from the volunteer page: a 2-hour orientation, at least three shifts of about 3 hours from May to October, and online booking. The farm page gives no volunteer day details, so those come from the calendar listings for Oct 10, Oct 24 and Nov 14, 2026 (each 9:30 am to noon). The calendar page read back some odd old header dates, so its listings were checked against the volunteer page. The season tag 'summer' from tier 1 was removed, since the volunteer days and Welcome Center run into autumn. The visit page names no SEPTA line or stop, so nearest SEPTA is left out. The volunteer page says its contact link does not work, so the phone number is used. The minimum age of 18 is the sign-up age; minors may take part with a parent or guardian.

records.name: Batikh Batikh
records.summary: A free cinema and gallery collective that screens films from Southwest Asia and North Africa and helps women and queer artists put on solo shows.
records.what_you_do: Go to a free screening or exhibition when one is announced. Artists who want to show can email the collective about an open call, with the call's name in the subject line.

schedule.text: No fixed schedule is published. Screenings and exhibitions are announced on the site when they are set.

cost.text: All art shown is free to see.

first_step.how: Check the site for the next screening or exhibition and come along, or email the collective to ask where the next one is held.
first_step.basis: Screenings and shows are free and open to anyone, and the group has an email contact and an Instagram account. The site gives no venue address and no dated screenings.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a visit or give a venue address, so email the collective before you plan a trip. Everything shown is free to see.
first_visit_tips: Email batikhbatikhcollective@gmail.com to ask where and when the next screening is held.
Follow the group's Instagram account, since the website has no mailing list or calendar.
Accessibility details, such as step-free entry or captions, are not listed, so ask by email.

records.notes: The site lists no current screenings. Three past screenings and one current exhibition are named, but none has a date or year. Status stays probably_active because the site works and has no dated evidence. No venue address appears anywhere on the site. Open calls: seven themed calls plus a rolling call, with no deadlines and no submission fee; acceptance is not guaranteed. The home page says featured artists are paid, while the open calls page gives no artist fee. Re-check in about three months for dated events.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Orchard Project
leads_only.note: Named on Awbury's site as the host of the food forest work day listings. Its events page was read for this batch (Awbury's Oct 14 and Penn Park's Oct 28, 2026 workdays). Its own about and volunteer pages were not read, so it still needs its own record.

leads_only.name: Glen Foerd
leads_only.note: Named on Audubon's Mid-Atlantic page as the host of a Philly Birding Weekend kayak and birdwatch event. Not checked.
